summary: ARES (Adaptive Reconnaissance & Expedition System) turns real NASA data into a metre-scale plan for a suited Marswalk at Jezero Crater. It layers HiRISE terrain and imagery, CRISM spectral indices and MOLA elevation, screens the ground for slope and hazards, and picks three science stops: olivine-, hydrated-silicate- and carbonate-index terrain. It then plans a least-cost walking loop from a habitat: 9.24 km, an estimated 4.17-hour EVA inside an assumed 8-hour limit, steepest slope 8.2 degrees, farthest walk-back 4.62 km. We checked the hazard map against 261 real Perseverance waypoints (0.8% fall in our no-go terrain, which covers 1.7% of the map) and show the nearest rover image at each stop. A cinematic mission replay and an open notebook let anyone explore or reproduce the results. It matters because astronauts will walk, and global maps cannot tell a crew where to go safely. ARES is a planning prototype, not a certified safe route, and labels every output as measured, derived or assumed.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

ARES (Adaptive Reconnaissance & Expedition System) plans a suited Marswalk at Jezero Crater from real NASA data. Our notebook downloads NASA HiRISE terrain and imagery, CRISM spectral indices and MOLA elevation, validates each file, and registers them in one Mars coordinate frame. It computes slope and a hazard fraction at a 10 m planning grid, marks no-go ground (slope above 20 degrees or dense steep pixels), selects three science stops from quality-masked CRISM indices (olivine, hydrated silicate, carbonate), and plans a least-cost walking loop from a habitat using a relative walking-effort cost. In our run the loop is 9.24 km with three stops, an estimated 4.17-hour EVA inside an assumed 8-hour limit, a steepest slope of 8.2 degrees and a farthest walk-back of 4.62 km.

We then ground the plan in real surface data. We compared the hazard map with 261 NASA Perseverance waypoints inside the map: 0.8% fall in our no-go terrain, which covers 1.7% of the area. We also show the nearest Perseverance image at the habitat and each stop, with its distance. A web mission replay animates the walk with live distance, EVA clock, slope, walk-back and reference dose readouts, and lets a viewer toggle no-go zones and the rover's real path.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Global Mars portals show regional scale; a crew on foot needs metre-scale decisions. ARES shows where a crew can walk, what is worth the walk, how long it takes, how far home is, and what the ground looks like on arrival. The same route, no-go mask and budget are plain rasters and JSON, so they could drive a habitat display, a tablet or a helmet HUD. The pipeline is reusable: changing the product IDs targets another site.

TOOLS

Python (rasterio, GDAL, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-image, pandas, matplotlib) in a Kaggle notebook; HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the replay site; GitHub for the code and Render for hosting. Data: MRO HiRISE and CRISM and MGS MOLA from NASA PDS; Mars 2020 raw images, rover waypoints and MEDA weather from NASA.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

We fuse spectral science targets with a metre-scale safety and effort budget, test our own hazard model against where a real rover drove, and present the result as a replayable mission instead of a static map. Every output is labelled measured, derived or assumed.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Safety: no-go terrain, walk-back distance, EVA time and a reference radiation dose. Cost and energy: free, open NASA data and free tools; the site is a static page with no server computation. Accessibility: the site respects reduced-motion settings and uses readable contrast.

HONEST LIMITS

ARES is a planning prototype, not a certified safe route. Thresholds, walking speed and the EVA limit are our assumptions. We do not model suit mass, Mars gravity, rock-scale hazards, thermal loads or live space weather. The radiation figure uses a published reference rate, not a Jezero measurement. CRISM indices show where to look, not confirmed minerals. The rover is not a suited astronaut, and the rover check rests on a small count.
